positiveControls.result: N(t)=1000/(1+9e^(−0.6t)), t≥0, is displayed consistently. N(0)=100 and 0<N(t)<1000 hold. The marked start has coordinates (110,542), exactly 33 pixels above zero on a 165-pixel 0→500 interval.

The plotted N-axis ticks 0,100,250,500,750,1000 all use py=575−0.33N. The t-axis ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10 all use px=110+74t. All 1001 graph samples agree with the displayed function to sub-0.0005-pixel coordinate rounding.

N'=0.6N(1−N/1000)>0. N''=0.6N'(1−2N/1000), hence curvature changes at N=500. t_W=ln(9)/0.6≈3.66204; the point lies before t=4 and at the exact 500 level. The blue curve rises first with increasing and then decreasing slope.
0.6N(1−N/1000) is a downward-opening quadratic in N, maximized at N=500. Its value there is 150; the text explicitly says absolute growth per model time unit, not maximal relative growth.
The horizontal dashed K=1000 line uses the same y-scale. The graph remains below it for finite t; N(10)=978.17805 is visibly below the line. The model approaches 1000 from below as t grows.
E(t)=100exp(0.6t) has the same initial value 100, E'=0.6E>0 and E''=0.36E>0. Growth is proportional to stock, the curve becomes steeper and has no inflection or finite upper bound.

B(t)=1000−900exp(−0.6t) has initial value 100 and cap 1000; B'=540exp(−0.6t)=0.6(1000−B)>0 and B''=−324exp(−0.6t)<0. It becomes flatter and has no inflection, including at t=0. The false parenthetical is absent.

L(t)=N(t) unambiguously refers to the main worked model. Its growth depends on stock and remaining carrying capacity; the final prompt asks the learner to check resources, stock and time period rather than treating the formula as a universal natural law.

The orange marker and dashed projections identify W, the blue marker/callout identifies N(0), and the orange horizontal dashed line identifies carrying capacity. No additional unverified inset curves occur. Formula exponent, fraction, inequalities, arrows, model comparisons and captions are readable in the actual PNG. No SVG text extends outside the 1600x900 viewport.
